name: Buffer Global in Browser
errorPattern: ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined
rootCause: Playwright Chromium browser runtime does not have Node.js Buffer in global scope.
rule: Guard 'instanceof Buffer' with 'typeof Buffer !== "undefined" && value instanceof Buffer' and use TextEncoder fallback for Buffer.from().
commentTemplate:
// In browser environments (Playwright Chromium under Vitest), Buffer is not globally defined.
// Guard with typeof Buffer !== 'undefined' to prevent: ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined.

name: Chained it().timeout() on Vitest
errorPattern: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined \(reading 'timeout'\)
rootCause: In Vitest, it() returns void, whereas in Mocha it returns a Test object. Calling it('...', fn).timeout(ms) throws TypeError.
rule: Pass timeout as the 3rd argument in it('name', fn, ms) and guard this.timeout inside functions with 'if (this && typeof this.timeout === "function") this.timeout(ms)'.
commentTemplate:
// In Vitest it() returns void (Mocha returns Test object). Chaining .timeout() throws:
// 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'timeout')'.

name: Mocha this.test.fullTitle() in Vitest Context
errorPattern: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined \(reading 'fullTitle'\)
rootCause: Vitest TestContext does not populate this.test like Mocha does.
rule: Replace this.test.fullTitle() with this?.test?.fullTitle() ?? '<fallback>'.
commentTemplate:
// Vitest TestContext does not populate this.test like Mocha.
// Use this?.test?.fullTitle() ?? '<fallback>' to prevent TypeError.

name: CommonJS require() in Native ESM
errorPattern: ReferenceError: require is not defined
rootCause: Vitest browser executes in native ESM where require() is not defined.
rule: Convert 'const config = require("path/to/project.json")' to 'import config from "path/to/project.json"'.
commentTemplate:
// Vitest browser runs in native ESM where require() is undefined.
// Use ESM import to avoid ReferenceError: require is not defined.

name: Floating Promise Unhandled Rejection
errorPattern: Unhandled Rejection: (.*)
rootCause: Vitest registers an unhandledRejection listener on window. Fire-and-forget promises that intentionally fail (e.g. pingServer, enqueueAndForget) bubble to window unless caught.
rule: Add .catch(() => {}) to background/fire-and-forget promise chains.
commentTemplate: // Catch network/simulated errors so offline servers don't trigger unhandled promise rejections in Vitest.

name: Prototype Augmentation Not Loaded
errorPattern: is not a function|undefined is not a function
rootCause: In Karma/Webpack, side-effect prototype extensions were eagerly evaluated. In Vitest ESM, prototype augmentations must be explicitly imported in test setup or test utilities.
rule: Explicitly import the implementation module (e.g. '../../src/api/pipeline_impl') in the test utility file.
commentTemplate: // Explicitly import module to ensure prototype augmentations are loaded in isolated ESM mode.

name: Native ESM Module Mocking in Vitest Browser
errorPattern: TypeError: Cannot redefine property|TypeError: ES Modules cannot be stubbed|Cannot spy on export
rootCause: In native ESM (Vite/Vitest browser mode), imported module namespaces are sealed/frozen objects. Both sinon.stub and vi.spyOn fail with 'Cannot redefine property' or 'ES Modules cannot be stubbed'. Module-level mocks must use vi.mock() with vi.hoisted() mock functions.
rule: Use 'const { mockFn } = vi.hoisted(() => ({ mockFn: vi.fn() })); vi.mock("path", async importOriginal => ({ ...(await importOriginal()), targetFn: (...args) => mockFn(...args) }));'.
commentTemplate: // In native ESM (Vitest browser), module namespaces are sealed. Use vi.mock() + vi.hoisted() for module mocking.

name: CommonJS Mocha Node Test Compatibility with Vitest
errorPattern: Error: Vitest cannot be imported in a CommonJS module using require\(\)
rootCause: When running 'yarn test:node' with ts-node in CommonJS mode, top-level 'import { vi } from "vitest"' compiles to require("vitest"), which throws because Vitest does not support CJS require().
rule: Do not import { vi } from 'vitest' in test files. Instead: 1) Add src/types/vitest-globals.d.ts with ambient global vi and Chai matcher declarations; 2) Add test/setup.mocha.ts shim providing globalThis.vi fallback and chai matchers; 3) Set 'test:node' script with 'TS_NODE_FILES=true TS_NODE_CACHE=NO' and '--require test/setup.mocha.ts'.
commentTemplate: // Avoid importing { vi } from 'vitest' directly in test files to preserve Mocha CommonJS test:node compatibility.

name: Clean Browser Global Environment (No Artificial Process Shim)
errorPattern: typeof process !== 'undefined'|Environment detection false positive
rootCause: Injecting artificial globalThis.process into the browser test runner pollutes global scope and causes packages that detect runtime environment via 'typeof process !== "undefined"' or 'process.env' to incorrectly assume they are running in Node.js.
rule: Do not inject synthetic process or process.env onto globalThis in browser test setups. Keep browser test runner global scope clean and native.
commentTemplate: // Do not inject synthetic process onto globalThis in browser test runners to ensure environment detection remains accurate.

name: Lockfile Pinning over Package.json Resolutions
errorPattern: TypeError: s.stringWidth is not a function|Yarn resolutions clutter
rootCause: Adding top-level 'resolutions' blocks to monorepo package.json clutters project configuration and introduces workspace-wide overrides. In Yarn 1.x workspaces, transient dependency conflicts (e.g. CommonJS string-width on Node 22) should be resolved and pinned directly in yarn.lock.
rule: Resolve transitive dependency version constraints directly in yarn.lock to keep root package.json minimal and clean.
commentTemplate: // Pin transitive dependency versions directly in yarn.lock rather than polluting package.json.

name: ESM Module Stubbing on Global Defaults
errorPattern: TypeError: ES Modules cannot be stubbed
rootCause: In Native ESM, imported module namespaces are sealed and immutable (Object.isFrozen === true), preventing sinon.stub from rewriting exported functions.
rule: Use global object property manipulation (or Object.defineProperty) instead of sinon.stub on imported ESM namespaces.
commentTemplate:
// Define throwing property or assign __FIREBASE_DEFAULTS__ on global instead of stubbing module exports
// to avoid native ESM error: "TypeError: ES Modules cannot be stubbed"

name: Avoid Shadowing Node.js Global Variable
errorPattern: import \* as global from|global\.getGlobal\(\)
rootCause: Importing a module namespace as 'global' (e.g., 'import * as global from "../src/global"') shadows the Node.js global variable 'global', causing confusion and subtle bugs.
rule: Never import a module namespace as 'global'. Use named imports like 'import { getGlobal } from "../src/global"'.

name: Avoid Stubbing process.env to Undefined in Node.js
errorPattern: stub\(process, ['"]env['"]\)\.value\(undefined\)
rootCause: Stubbing process.env to undefined in Node.js is risky because Node.js internals, Vitest reporters, and async hooks depend on process.env being an object. Vitest runs tests in both Node and native Browser Chromium; browser tests naturally cover the 'typeof process === "undefined"' branch without needing synthetic stubs in Node.
rule: Do not stub process.env to undefined in Node tests. Rely on native browser test execution to verify environments where process is undefined, and delete individual environment keys if needed.

name: Resolved Error: ReferenceError: global is not defined...
errorPattern: ReferenceError: global is not defined
rootCause: Browser environments under Playwright Chromium do not define Node.js global variable. Accessing global.__FIREBASE_DEFAULTS__ throws ReferenceError in browser.
rule: Replace global.<var> with globalThis.<var> for cross-platform browser/node global access in tests.

name: Resolved Error: TypeError: Cannot spy on export .* Modul...
errorPattern: TypeError: Cannot spy on export .* Module namespace is not configurable in ESM
rootCause: In native ESM (Vitest browser mode), imported module namespaces are sealed and unconfigurable (Object.isFrozen === true).
rule: Stub class prototype or instance methods instead of trying to stub sealed ESM module exports.

name: Resolved Error: State leakage from globalThis mutation...
errorPattern: State leakage from globalThis mutation
rootCause: Setting globalThis properties in tests without a try...finally block leaves global state mutated if an assertion fails.
rule: Wrap test logic in try...finally to ensure globalThis cleanups always execute.

name: Resolved Error: Suite-level stubs cleaned up early by gl...
errorPattern: Suite-level stubs cleaned up early by global afterEach restore
rootCause: Calling sinon.stub in beforeAll is undone after the first test if a global afterEach calls sinon.restore().
rule: Use a dedicated sandbox (createSandbox()) for suite-level stubs and restore it in afterAll.

name: Resolved Error: Silent test pass with 0 assertions in No...
errorPattern: Silent test pass with 0 assertions in Node
rootCause: Wrapping entire test body in if (isFeatureAvailable()) causes test to pass silently with 0 assertions in unsupported environments.
rule: Use it.skipIf(!isFeatureAvailable()) so the test runner properly reports the test as skipped.

name: Preserve Const Enums in Rollup Build for ESM Consumer Compatibility
errorPattern: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '.*')|is not exported by
rootCause: TypeScript const enums are stripped at compile time unless preserveConstEnums: true is enabled in compilerOptions. When downstream packages run under Vitest/Vite in native ESM mode, the imported enum object is undefined at runtime.
rule: If a package exports a const enum used across the monorepo, ensure its rollup.config.js includes compilerOptions: { preserveConstEnums: true } in typescriptPlugin.

name: Do Not Place Ambient Test Typings in src/ Directory
errorPattern: ae-missing-release-tag|assert_2|polluted API extractor
rootCause: Placing vitest-globals.d.ts inside src/ causes api-extractor during yarn build to analyze it as part of the public TypeScript program, generating unwanted diffs and symbol aliasing (e.g. assert renamed to assert_2) in common/api-review/*.api.md.
rule: Never place vitest-globals.d.ts inside src/. Keep ambient test typings in test/types/ or rely on config/vitest.base.mjs globals: true.

name: ESM_BROWSER_MODULE_STUB_DELEGATOR
errorPattern: TypeError: ES Modules cannot be stubbed|Cannot spy on export
rootCause: In native browser (Playwright Chromium) and Vite ESM execution, namespace objects from import * as mod are non-configurable and sealed. sinon.stub(mod, 'prop') fails because exports are read-only getters.
rule: Hoist mock delegator with vi.hoisted(() => ({ mockTarget: { fn: (..._args: any[]) => {} } })), vi.mock(modulePath, () => delegator), and stub(mod, method) routing to sinonStub(mockTarget, method) so Sinon sandbox automatically tracks and restores it via standard sinon.restore().
commentTemplate: // Module export stubbing in native ESM browser runner: use vi.hoisted mock delegator with sinonStub(mockTarget, method)

name: Normalize Node-specific global to standard globalThis in tests
errorPattern: ReferenceError: global is not defined
rootCause: In native browser (Playwright Chromium) ESM test execution, Node.js global identifier is undefined. Using global directly (e.g. sinon.stub(global, ...)) causes ReferenceError.
rule: Replace global identifier with standard ECMAScript globalThis in test files via AST codemod.

name: Migrate Mocha early return and this.skip() to Vitest conditional runners
errorPattern: TypeError: this.skip is not a function|Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'skip')
rootCause: In Vitest, arrow functions in tests lose Mocha this context, and early returns inside describe() blocks still execute hooks. this.skip() throws TypeError.
rule: Rewrite describe blocks with early returns to (condition ? describe.skip : describe) and this.skip() guards to (condition ? it : it.skip).

name: Sinon Fake Timers Background Polling Leaks
errorPattern: clock.runAll.*leaked retry|waitUntilFidRegistration.*timeout
rootCause: In afterEach, calling clock.runAll() fast-forwards fake timers past polling timeout thresholds, triggering retry loops that leak unhandled promises and rogue state into subsequent tests.
rule: Do not call clock.runAll() in afterEach; use clock.restore() to safely discard pending timers. In tests with polling loops, advance only the necessary time and ensure loops conclude before test exits.
commentTemplate: // Avoid clock.runAll() in afterEach when background polling loops are active to prevent timeout triggers and async leaks.

name: Migrate legacy Sinon-Chai mock assertions to native Vitest matchers
errorPattern: Sinon-Chai assertions left in code|calledOnce|toHaveBeenCalledTimes|toHaveBeenCalledWith|has\.been\.calledWith
rootCause: Migrating from Sinon to Vitest mocks leaves legacy Sinon-Chai assertions (.to.have.been.calledOnce, .has.been.calledWith, .to.have.been.called, .to.not.have.been.called). While Vitest provides a compatibility layer, PR reviewers and automated bots (e.g. Gemini Code Assist) flag them as obsolete or non-idiomatic.
rule: Convert legacy Sinon-Chai assertions to native Vitest mock assertions: .calledOnce -> toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1), .calledTwice -> toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2), .calledThrice -> toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3), .called -> toHaveBeenCalled(), .not.have.been.called -> not.toHaveBeenCalled(), and .calledWith(...) -> toHaveBeenCalledWith(...).
